Sixteen comments

“Blacksmith’s”

A simple reel, which I first heard played by the Cork trio “Na Fili” on John Peel’s late night programme sometime in the early 70s.
[ I haven’t listened to him in years, but at that time he was having people such as “Na Fili”, the “Chieftains”, “Planxty”, “Boys Of The Lough” , the JSD Band , the Fureys , and even John Doonan as guests on his programme – on Radio 1, albeit ,in a late night spot. A few years ago, he gave over half of his programme to a live set from Sharon Shannon. Peel’s one of the good guys. ]
“The Blacksmith’s” I would say was made popular in Scotland at that time by Tony Cuffe, who recorded it solo, and also with the group “Alba".

↳ Posted by Kenny on October 5th, 2004.

I like this tune and I don’t know why. I love the way it doesn’t go anywhere. It just keeps going cyclically back into itself. It’d make a good middle tune in a set of 3, maybe with 2 tunes that use a wider pitch range.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on December 8th, 2006.

Matt Cranitch’s

This feature’s on an album from the Temple House Céilí Band: Music for Sets Vol. 1. They call it Matt Cranitch’s.

↳ Posted by Paahto on January 10th, 2007.

London Bridge/The Blacksmith’s

I’ve been enjoying listening to Micho Russell’s “Traditional Irish Music From County Clare”. One tune which has taken my fancy is “London Bridge”:

X:1
T:London Bridge
S:Micho Russell
Z:Nigel Gatherer
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
G2 GG DGBG | G2 Bd cAFA | G2 GG DGBG | AFDF ABcA |
Gz G2 DGBG | G2 Bd cAFA | d2 cA BGAF | DEED Acdc :|
d2 B2 dBGB | dB B2 deed | dB B2 dBGB | AFDF ABcA |
d2 B2 dBGB | dB B2 deed | d2 cA BGAF | DEED ABcA :|

Having studied the tunes in the database, this would appear to be related to “The Blacksmith’s Reel” although there are significant differences. I’m not sure whether to keep this tune here with its alternative title, or whether it should be entered as a tune on its own. Any opinions?

Re: The Blacksmith’s

Recorded March 19, 1923, by Dublin piper Billy Andrews: https://archive.org/details/01HornpipeTheRakesOfKildareTheBlacksmith

It’s in Ceol Rince na hEireann vol. I, taken from the playing of Breandan’s piping uncle Saosamh Breathnach. Obviously a tune for the big pipes. Andrews played both instruments, and a recording of him playing the warpipes survives.

↳ Posted by What's the name of this tune? on September 21st, 2024.
